newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Thursday on profit-taking after sharp gains in the previous session, traders said.
The key Janaury 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 3,140 yuan ($378) per tonne, down 90 yuan. It opened at a high of 3,230.
March fell 30 to 3,100, May rose 30 to 3,170, July was up 20 to 3,220, September dropped 60 to 3,350 and November 30 to 3,350.
Combined volume fell to 17,300 tonnes from 28,500.
Traders said profit-taking was responsible for today's falls.
"Tuesday's sharp gains made many investors want to take their profits today," one trader said. "But many investors remain on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news."
Analysts expect soybeans to consolidate around the current levels in the next few days.
